I understand you're asking about the common symptoms of bladder cancer.

The most common symptom of bladder cancer is blood in the urine, also known as hematuria . The urine may appear slightly rusty or bright red . This symptom occurs in about 90% of bladder cancer cases . In some instances, hematuria can be intermittent . Other symptoms can include frequent urination, needing to urinate at night (nocturia), and pain or burning during urination (dysuria) .

If you notice blood in your urine, it's important to see a doctor as soon as possible. Even if the blood disappears, get it checked out. I understand you're asking about lymphoma staging.

The stage of lymphoma describes how far the cancer has spread in the body. Doctors use a system called the Lugano classification to stage lymphoma . You might hear about an "E" designation, which means the cancer started in tissues outside the main lymphatic areas but nearby. Stage IV means the lymphoma has spread widely to an extranodal site, like the liver .

To figure out the stage, doctors use various tests, including a CT scan, biopsy, and staging workup . A key warning sign of lymphoma is a lump or mass .
